subject: phoenix
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: phoenix with flame plumage, wings spread.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a phoenix module in a Genshin-style cel-shaded aesthetic, in a rest pose with spread wings standing on a small brazier base with ornate gold trim and glowing flames, aiming to keep the implementation compact at around 400 lines while using the available rendering utilities carefully.

Now I'm laying out the skeleton: a hip root joint with a spine chain curving up to the chest, then a neck chain of catmull points rising to the head, defining parent relationships and joint names for each segment while making sure the base sits flush at ground level and the bird's proportions stay around 1.4m tall with a 3m wingspan.

I'm working through the tail next, chaining three curved segments backward and downward from the hips, with feather sweeps planned as gradient-colored bezier shapes attached to the tail bones. Then I'm figuring out the body mesh itself, considering whether to sweep the spine chain directly to connect tail, hips, and spine into one continuous form.

I'll use a countershading paint for the body, gold-to-orange gradient based on surface normal. For legs, I'm setting up a limb function from hip to foot with segment lengths and bend directions, working out how the reach distances and bend counts need to match up across three segments.

Still planning the leg chain naming, toe placement via spikes off the foot joint, and now moving on to designing the wing arm chains from the shoulder.

Designing the feather outline and gradient paint...

Still working out feather layout...

Wings stay flat with slight dihedral, thin extruded prisms. I'm tallying feather counts per wing layer plus tail and head crest feathers, then writing a paint helper function that colors each feather along its length with a gradient.

I need to confirm mix is exported from the SDK for blending colors, and I'm weighing whether to cache paints by rounding length values to avoid redundant paint objects per feather, since recomputing per-feather is cheap enough anyway.

For glow, I'm realizing it doesn't apply well to painted surfaces, so instead I should add it to flame-like elements separately—extruding yellow flame shapes with glow applied as flat color for the crown crest, tail tips, and base fire. I'm sketching out a teardrop-shaped flame outline function with width and height parameters to generate these flame wisps as distinct geometry.

For the base fire, I'll arrange a ring of flame extrusions standing upright around the brazier, oriented tangent to the circle, glowing yellow-orange. I also want to add an emblem decal on the pedestal—a Pyro-style flame-and-circle symbol drawn in gold on red as a textured plane, mounted on a stepped lathe pedestal base.

Now I'm scaling the pedestal with a wider bottom radius and narrower top, placing the bird on top with a gold rim torus and small flames around the edge. I'm adding floating ember spheres as small glowing octahedra fixed to the root bone, and working out the pedestal attachment at the hips joint, then building the head with a sphere and cone-shaped beak parts.

Adding beak and jaw geometry...

For the eyes, I'll decal an orange iris with highlight onto the head sphere using surface placement around the head's center, positioning them at a mirrored azimuth so left and right eyes sit symmetrically on the sides, sized to fit the sphere's radius without overlapping the beak.

Now I'm working out the crest, using a feather helper to extrude five flame-like feathers from the top-back of the head, with varying directions and lengths to create a fan shape, adjusting the "up" reference so the feather planes face outward nicely when viewed from the side or top.

Then I'm planning the tail: seven feathers fanning back and downward from the tail root with graduated lengths (longest in the center), plus two extra-long ribbon plumes that sweep using bezier curves with flame styling.

Writing bezier sweep code...

Then I'm working through the up-vector orientation issue — for tail feathers I need the blade flat horizontally (outline spread front-to-back), but using up=[0,1,0] instead produces a vertical fin-like blade, which is wrong for wings where I want the flat horizontal orientation.

Now I'm working out the wing geometry: feather direction vectors get a slight upward rise component for dihedral, with root positions pulled from the arm chain's parametric points, and I'm setting up the leading edge sweep for the wing.

Adding covert feather layers and sizing out the span—arm length around 1.6 per side, span over 3.4, primaries about 1.1 long—then fanning feather roots along the arm from hand to shoulder for primaries and secondaries separately.

Defining feather color gradients...

Checking the tip points don't self-intersect, then moving to body details — thinking about adding a gold collar around the neck using a torus shape positioned along the neck's tangent direction at roughly a quarter of the way along its sweep.

I'll also add small gold ornaments: a tiny red glowing jewel on the forehead, gold anklets as tori at the ankles, and gold bracelets at the wrists for that Genshin-style look. For the main body, I'm setting up a spine chain sweep from hips to chest with varying radii to shape the torso naturally.

I'm tapering the tail sweep to a point with feathers at the end, narrowing the neck sweep, and making sure the spine chain starts exactly at the hip joint. For the legs, I'm positioning the hip joints within the body radius and working out leg lengths so the feet land correctly on the base platform.

For the limb chains, I'm setting up each leg as four points (hip, knee, ankle, foot) forming three segments plus the tip, which the chain function can take directly as a polyline. I'm naming each joint per side and assigning the "leg" role, then sweeping the leg geometry with a gold scale color, and adding feathered trouser spheres at the thighs in orange.

Now I'm adding toes: from the foot endpoint, I'm spiking out three forward toes plus a back toe using direction vectors that get normalized, coloring them gold and anchoring them to the leg's tip bone, with small adjustments to the foot's y-position so the toes sit naturally into the base without clipping too far below it.

Then I'm lathing the stone pedestal with a profile outline that flares out at the base and tapers upward with a slight lip, anchored to the hip bone, and I'm planning to paint it with a mottled stone texture in deep purples and grays reminiscent of a Pyro-aligned Liyue aesthetic.

For the top, I'll add a thin gold torus ring and a circle of eight stylized flames alternating orange and yellow around the rim, leaning outward with the bird positioned at the center, making sure feet and tail feathers clear the flame geometry.

I'm checking the tail droop trajectory to confirm it stays clear of the flame ring and pedestal edges as it curves down and back, then planning the pedestal's front emblem placement, angling a small plane along the sloped side face to match the pedestal's radius at that height.

For the emblem itself, I'm sketching an SVG design: a dark circular background with a gold ring stroke and a stylized flame shape in red/orange at the center.

I'm deciding against adding a sun-disc halo behind the phoenix to avoid cluttering the wings, but planning some floating glowing embers scattered around for atmosphere. I'm also thinking through chest details -- a small ruff of downward-pointing feathers extruded at the front of the chest for extra visual texture.

Placing roots at the chest surface with yellow-white plumes. Setting head position with a sphere radius and gold-orange beak color with a darker tip, estimating overall model height around 1.9 units. Now working out the wing rig chains, defining shoulder joints and naming the chain points.

I'm correcting the side convention so s=1 maps to left (+X), and planning a feather helper function that extrudes an outline along a given direction using a cross product to compute the perpendicular axis, making sure to avoid degenerate cases where the normal and direction vectors align.

I'm also setting up a paint caching system keyed by color and length, adding a subtle golden shaft line down the center of each feather for visual detail, and preparing the tail chain by sampling joint positions along its length for root and bone placement.

Now I'm laying out a nine-feather fan spanning -40 to 40 degrees, with the center feather longest and tapering toward the edges, using layered colors (red, orange, yellow) with gold accents at the center. I'm also adding curling ribbon plumes via bezier curves sweeping from the tail root outward, checking tip positions stay clear of the floor near the pedestal.

Writing sweep code for ribbon with gradient colors and pointed caps, plus a glow effect at the ribbon tip. I'm deciding to skip wing tip flames but considering small flame wisps near the wrist, and thinking about whether to add a crest of flames along the back before moving to countershading for the body material.

Now I'm setting up the toon shading and imports from the kit, then starting the builder code, defining the hips joint as the spine root and building out the spine chain with a catmull curve through several points.

Continuing into the neck chain, parenting it to the spine's last joint, then setting up the head joint parented to the neck with its own position and direction vector.

Now I'm defining the body sweep radii along the spine, a smaller sweep for the neck, and considering a rump sphere near the hips before deciding whether to add a tail sweep.

For details, I'm adding gold wrist bracelets as tori oriented along the arm bone's tangent, setting up cel-shaded color fills for the body, tail, and thigh tufts using countershading, and scattering small glowing octahedron embers around the hips at varying radii and heights for a magical effect.

Now I'm placing a ring of nine flame shapes around the pedestal base, extruding them radially with alternating heights and colors and a moderate glow, then starting on five crest feathers rooted near the top of the head.

I'm adjusting the jewel's position slightly so it sits properly on the sphere's surface without clipping through, settling on a small pink octahedron offset upward. For the head itself, I'm going with a cel-shaded orange-to-yellow countershade sphere with gold cheeks, and setting up the eye decals to target the head mesh.

I'm working through helper logic for mirroring parts across the center axis and sizing the eyes relative to the head radius, then setting an orange-red iris color. For the beak I'll skip adding nostril detail to keep things simple, and I still need to write the pedestal texture, emblem, and final export metadata. I'm also cleaning up TypeScript types, aliasing Vector3 for convenience and writing a helper to convert plain coordinate arrays into proper vector instances.

Now I'm writing the wing-building code, generating mirrored left/right point arrays, building a smooth curve through shoulder/elbow/wrist/hand joints, and sweeping a tapered tube along it with rounded caps—then defining a reusable layering function for feather generation...

Checking the proportions—the wingspan was coming out too large relative to the bird's height, so I'm scaling down the arm length points and tip lengths to bring the span to around 4.5-5.2m against a 1.7m height, which feels more majestic without being oversized.

Now defining the tail feather geometry: positioning the root at the tail's quarter point, computing feather direction vectors based on angle, and setting up the tail joint chain from the hips back through decreasing heights to reach the tail tip around z=-1.8.

Working through the toe and anklet placement, I'm confirming that the leg IK returns Vector3 points so I can safely reference the last joint for spike bases and use the second joint for an anklet torus oriented along the z-axis.

Writing the final joint and geometry code...
